items.label: f01-four-concerns
items.front: The four concerns in markNotificationOpenedForSession, in order
items.back: Ownership (292-296, 404 unless view:any or recipient); lifecycle (298-304, 409 unless a SENT delivery; repeated in SQL); aggregation (308 -> refresh at 57-71); audit (310-318). No transaction wraps the writes.

items.label: f02-notification-derivation
items.back: No deliveries -> QUEUED; all in {SENT, OPENED, SKIPPED} -> COMPLETED; all in {FAILED, SKIPPED} -> FAILED; some delivered and some FAILED -> PARTIAL_FAILURE; else PROCESSING if any PROCESSING, otherwise QUEUED.

items.label: f03-retry-forever
items.front: Why transient delivery failures retry forever
items.back: markDeliveryDeferred never increments attemptCount, so nextAttemptCount is always 1, exhausted never becomes true and backoff stays at one minute. Fix: increment attemptCount for RETRYING (not RATE_LIMITED).

items.prompt: How does refreshNotificationAndBatchState update the batch after an open?

choices.text: It copies the notification's new status onto the batch row
It adds one to the batch's opened counter for the new open
It leaves the batch untouched until the worker's next polling run
It re-derives the batch status from all its notification statuses

choices: It copies the notification's new status onto the batch row
It adds one to the batch's opened counter for the new open
It leaves the batch untouched until the worker's next polling run
It re-derives the batch status from all its notification statuses

items.explanation: It reads every delivery status of the notification, derives and writes the notification status, then reads every notification status of the batch and derives the batch status: recomputed from scratch, never incremented.

items.prompt: Every notification in a batch is PARTIAL_FAILURE. What does deriveBatchStatus return?

choices.text: PARTIAL_FAILURE, the same status every notification has
PROCESSING, since the batch has not finished delivering
QUEUED, since no branch matches without a COMPLETED one
FAILED, as none of the notifications fully completed

choices: PARTIAL_FAILURE, the same status every notification has
PROCESSING, since the batch has not finished delivering
QUEUED, since no branch matches without a COMPLETED one
FAILED, as none of the notifications fully completed

items.explanation: The PARTIAL_FAILURE branch needs at least one COMPLETED notification; all-COMPLETED and all-FAILED do not match either, and with no PROCESSING the fallback is QUEUED. The review lists it as a real mislabel.
